title: Sick day management in people with chronic kidney disease: a scoping review
authors: Duong H, Tesfaye W, Van C, Sud K, Truong M, Krass I, et al.
population: Ten studies and seven guidelines on temporary medication discontinuation during acute illness in people with chronic kidney disease
funder: Open Access funding enabled and organized by CAUL and its Member Institutions. The authors declare that they have no relevant financial or other conflicts of interest.
authorConflicts: The authors declare that they have no relevant financial or other conflicts of interest.
result: Most guidelines recommended sick-day medication management, including temporary withholding of drugs that raise the risk of acute kidney injury, largely on expert consensus. There is little evidence on the effect of sick-day protocols on outcomes; a single randomised trial found no significant association between a sick-day protocol and change in kidney function, acute kidney injury or hospitalisation.
